book_title: Chapter 8: Anatomy of a Stage 4 Collapse Across Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Tapes
question: What do the 1W, 1D, and 4H charts, institutional volume spikes, and options chain confirm about NBIL as of November 20, 2026?

epigraph.quote: Never try to catch a falling knife—especially when the blade is sharpened by 2x daily leverage and institutional distribution.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis Principle

web_blocks.html: NBIL's technical tape as of November 20, 2026 represents one of the cleanest Stage 4 Markdown collapses in the U.S. market [57][58]. Shares plunged -32.45% on Friday alone from $3.39 to $2.29, printing a fresh 52-week low of $2.25—a staggering -96.66% drawdown from the $68.49 peak [57]. Both the quantitative market_facts ledger and the TradingView snapshot classify NBIL unambiguously as STAGE_4 / CAP_REJECTED inside an S&P 500 Downtrend (10 distribution days; only 38.8% of stocks above 50-DMA; 0 of 9 sectors above 20-DMA) [57][58].

The multi-timeframe package confirms unbroken downward momentum across every trading horizon with zero bullish divergence [58]. On the Weekly (1W) frame, NBIL sits -91.37% below its 30-week SMA ($26.55) and -81.67% below its 10-week EMA ($12.49; daily proxy $13.84) with Weekly RSI at 34.67 [57][58]. On the Daily (1D) frame, price trades -85.70% below the falling 50-day SMA ($16.01, down from $23.66 twenty-one sessions ago) and -90.21% below the 200-day SMA ($23.40), with Daily RSI at 29.72 and ATR14 at $2.09 (91.3% of share price) [57][58]. On the 4-Hour (4H) intraday frame, intraday_4h_turn remains false: close ($2.29) sits well below the 4H EMA20 ($5.11) and 4H SMA50 ($8.60), with 4H RSI pinned at 26.63.

Crucially, Friday's close at $2.29 decisively breached our locked November 13 structural stop of $2.92—which also matches TradingView's Classic S1 Pivot ($2.92)—by -21.6% [57][58]. Daily volume exploded to 38.30 million shares in the facts ledger (2.33x 20-day average; 39.14 million / 2.66x 30-day average on TradingView; 4.80x Finviz relative volume vs. 8.15M avg) [57][58][59]. Note two minor data-feed differences disclosed transparently: TradingView reports rolling 1W/1M/3M returns of -59.75% / -83.51% / -91.12% versus facts-ledger/Finviz -53.74% / -79.55% / -89.75% due to trading-day windowing, and Finviz's static card still shows a stale 52W low of $3.36 compared to Friday's live $2.25 low [57][58][59].

web_blocks.title: Options Overlay Audit & Positions-Ledger Risk Anomaly

web_blocks.html: Although NBIL carries listed options, the November 20 options desk audit assigns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. The desk rule is explicit: never purchase rebound calls or call spreads on a security rated FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL in Pass 1. Because NBIL's 14-day ATR ($2.09) equals 91% of its share price, implied volatility premiums on any strike above $2.50 reflect extreme binary decay and wide retail spreads. Automated macOS Chrome inspection of Robinhood and TradingView tabs was unavailable in the Linux sandbox, so the options audit relies cleanly on public multi-timeframe and chain data.

Finally, our forensic audit caught an important data defect in the portfolio positions ledger. That ledger labels NBIL as CASH_EQUIV_ETF with leverage_multiplier: 0.0 and effective_beta: 0.0, under the legacy name T-Rowway 2X Long NBIS ETF. In reality, GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF carries 2.0x daily leverage and an observed Finviz Beta of 8.90 [59]. Even though the remaining 50.0 shares represent just 0.15% of portfolio net worth ($114.50 of $75,110.60), clearing that misclassified position immediately removes hidden tail beta from the Robinhood book.

book_paragraphs: Charts do not lie about capital flows, and NBIL's technical tape as of Friday, November 20, 2026 reads like a textbook autopsy of a Stage 4 collapse. In a single trading session, shares plunged thirty-two point four-five percent from three dollars and thirty-nine cents to two dollars and twenty-nine cents, carving a fresh fifty-two-week low of two dollars and twenty-five cents. From its peak of sixty-eight dollars and forty-nine cents, the exchange-traded fund has surrendered ninety-six point six-six percent of its market value.

When we inspect the multi-timeframe structure across weekly, daily, and four-hour candles, there is not a single pocket of technical support left beneath the price. On the weekly chart, NBIL sits ninety-one percent below its thirty-week simple moving average at twenty-six dollars and fifty-five cents and nearly eighty-two percent below its ten-week exponential moving average at twelve dollars and forty-nine cents. On the daily chart, the fifty-day moving average has rolled over sharply from twenty-three dollars and sixty-six cents to sixteen dollars and one cent in just twenty-one sessions.

Traders sometimes look at a daily Relative Strength Index reading of twenty-nine point seven-two and feel tempted to fish for a relief bounce. That impulse ignores the four-hour tape and the broader market regime. On the four-hour chart, the intraday turn flag remains false, with price trapped far beneath its four-hour twenty-period exponential average at five dollars and eleven cents and its RSI languishing at twenty-six point six-three. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 itself is locked in a ten-distribution-day downtrend with zero of nine sectors above their twenty-day averages.

Most decisively, Friday's slide sliced straight through our locked November 13 structural invalidation stop of two dollars and ninety-two cents—which also marked TradingView's S1 classic pivot—on thirty-eight point three million shares of volume, more than double the twenty-day average. In institutional risk management, a stop breach on heavy distribution volume terminates all debate.

From a strict Stan Weinstein market-cycle discipline, November 20, 2026 marks a textbook Stage 4 capitulation bar rather than an oversold bargain setup. Closing near the session low at $2.29 on more than double average volume demonstrates institutional liquidation pressure rather than quiet accumulation. Every key trend guidepost—the 20-day moving average, 50-day simple moving average, 10-week exponential average, 30-week simple average, and 200-day structural floor—slopes decisively downward miles overhead, creating heavy supply barriers on any reflex bounce.

Broad market regime data confirms that fighting broken individual momentum offers zero asymmetric edge right now. With only 38.8 percent of S&P 500 constituents holding above their 50-day moving average and ten institutional distribution days logged across the benchmark index, liquidity rewards defensive cash reserves and clean Stage 2 leaders rather than averaging down into high-ATR leveraged derivatives. Options volatility similarly offers no rescue because high implied premiums price wide daily swings rather than durable fundamental inflection.

book_subsections.title: Options Desk Discipline and the Positions-Ledger Classification Trap
paragraphs: Our options playbook confirms there is zero convex edge in trying to play a rebound through calls. The options desk enforces an iron rule: never buy rebound calls or debit spreads on a security whose underlying Pass 1 audit failed business quality standards. With fourteen-day Average True Range standing at two dollars and nine cents—ninety-one percent of the entire share price—option premiums and slippage would only compound losses.

During the technical audit, we also uncovered a subtle bookkeeping hazard inside the portfolio positions file. The file accidentally tags NBIL as a cash-equivalent ETF with zero leverage multiplier and zero effective beta under an outdated label. In truth, NBIL is GraniteShares' two-times daily leveraged NBIS fund carrying a Finviz beta of eight point nine-zero. Liquidating the remaining fifty shares corrects both the chart exposure and the hidden risk-budget distortion.

book_callouts.title: The Stage 4 Capitulation Rule: Never Average Down Below a Breached Stop
book_callouts.text: When a 2x daily ETF breaks its prior structural stop ($2.92) on >2.3x average volume and prints an ATR equal to 91% of its share price, low RSI is a symptom of forced liquidation, not a safe entry floor.
